chemistry.role: major phenolic monoterpenoid in many oregano oils

pharmacology.note: Mechanistic/preclinical evidence; not proof of systemic antimicrobial efficacy in humans.

records.scientific_name: Allium sativum L. — aged garlic extract
preparation: aged aqueous/ethanolic garlic extract; commercial preparations vary

chemistry.role: water-soluble sulfur compound commonly used as AGE marker
organosulfur compound reported in aged garlic

human_research.finding: 2026 systematic review/meta-analysis of 10 randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trials (n=625) found small, non-significant pooled changes in systolic/diastolic blood pressure.
Same 2026 analysis reported a significant pooled reduction in TNF-alpha, with heterogeneity across outcomes.
Triglycerides and cholesterol-related outcomes showed variable effects; do not equate biomarker changes with event prevention.

safety.hazard: do not generalize evidence from aged garlic extract to raw garlic or garlic essential oil

human_research.finding: 2024 systematic review/meta-analysis of six randomized trials (n=528) found increased risks of headache, nausea, anxiety, dizziness and elevated blood pressure at therapeutic doses; effects generally resolved within 48 hours.
2025 meta-analysis identified 9 RCTs / 602 participants; reporting quality and risk of bias varied substantially.

safety.hazard: rare serious adverse events in clinical literature
safety.note: Controlled clinical populations differ from unsupervised use.

human_research.finding: 2026 systematic review included 12 clinical trials / 174 participants; rapid onset and short duration were characteristic; no serious adverse events were reported in those controlled studies.
Controlled human studies report rapid, intense alterations in perception, cognition and self-experience.

safety.note: Risk is contextual and may be undercounted in controlled studies.

safety.hazard: oral aloe latex can cause abdominal pain, cramps and diarrhea
oral whole-leaf extracts have been associated with acute hepatitis reports

compounds.name: Harmine
compounds.notes: Major harmala alkaloid; potency and effects depend on preparation and context.

compounds.name: Harmaline
compounds.notes: Major harmala alkaloid with strong MAO-A relevance.

compounds.name: Tetrahydroharmine (THH)
compounds.notes: Major B. caapi constituent; pharmacology is more complex than simply classifying it as an MAOI.

compounds.name: N,N-Dimethyltryptamine (DMT)
compounds.notes: Pharmacology changes substantially when MAO inhibition is present.

compounds.name: N-Methyltryptamine (NMT)
compounds.notes: Reported as a minor P. viridis constituent.

compounds.name: 2-Methyl-1,2,3,4-tetrahydro-beta-carboline
compounds.notes: Reported minor constituent; human significance uncertain.

compounds.name: Nuciferine
compounds.notes: Occurs in Nymphaeaceae/Nelumbo literature; commercial blue-lotus composition is highly variable.

compounds.name: Apomorphine
compounds.notes: Pharmacologically active drug compound; attribution to authentic N. caerulea is disputed.

compounds.name: Thymoquinone
compounds.notes: Major N. sativa research compound; much evidence remains preclinical.

compounds.name: Carvacrol
compounds.notes: Strong preclinical antimicrobial literature; human clinical evidence is much narrower.

compounds.name: Thymol
compounds.notes: Common in oregano/thyme chemotypes.

compounds.name: Rosmarinic acid
compounds.notes: Common Lamiaceae constituent.

compounds.name: S-allyl-L-cysteine
compounds.notes: Characteristic marker/constituent of aged garlic preparations.

compounds.name: S-allyl-mercaptocysteine
compounds.notes: Reported in aged garlic extract.

compounds.name: Psilocybin
compounds.notes: Converted to psilocin after administration.

compounds.name: Psilocin
compounds.notes: Principal active metabolite responsible for classical serotonergic psychedelic effects.

compounds.name: Baeocystin
compounds.notes: Minor fungal alkaloid; independent human pharmacology remains uncertain.

compounds.name: Salvinorin A
compounds.notes: Potent non-nitrogenous KOR agonist.

compounds.name: Salvinorin B
compounds.notes: Major hydrolysis/metabolic product with much lower KOR activity.

compounds.name: Epicatechin
compounds.notes: Present in B. caapi alongside proanthocyanidins.

compounds.name: Procyanidin B2
compounds.notes: Reported B. caapi constituent.

compounds.name: Silymarin
compounds.notes: Principal standardized extract constituent of milk thistle; composition varies by preparation.

compounds.name: Hypericin
compounds.notes: Characteristic St. John's wort constituent; hyperforin and other constituents also contribute to pharmacology.

compounds.name: Withanolides
compounds.notes: Characteristic Withania constituents; preparations vary in withanolide content.

compounds.name: Boswellic acids
compounds.notes: Major resin constituents studied in Boswellia preparations; individual extracts differ.

interactions.mechanism: MAO inhibition can alter monoamine metabolism

interactions.risk: transient elevation reported in controlled trials

provenance_rule: Every substantive claim should point to one or more sources and one evidence level. Community and traditional sources remain queryable but are never silently promoted to clinical evidence.
safety_rule: Safety information is a first-class data type. Interaction warnings should be linked to agents, mechanisms, evidence level, and uncertainty rather than presented as generic disclaimers.

metadata.corpus_scope: Curated research corpus plus catalog seeds; not a claim of exhaustive global ethnobotanical coverage.
metadata.catalog_baseline: Historical UMMC guide plus Kew MPNS/POWO nomenclatural crosswalks.
metadata.safety_baseline: NCCIH, NIDDK LiverTox, systematic reviews and primary studies.
